claims.why: Checks that the correct measurement units are selected. Inspects connectors for moisture. Inspects connectors for dirt or damage. Checks for loose connections.
Dries the sensor port before installing the replacement sensor. Identifies compressed air as a port-drying option.
Warns that alcohol or other solvents can destroy the optical DO sensing surface. Warns that alcohol or other solvents can damage some plastics and o-rings.
Does not use the instrument until the warning's underlying error is identified, understood, and corrected.
Replaces damaged sensors. Recalibrates after replacing a damaged sensor.
Notes that battery performance decreases as temperature decreases. Carries spare batteries.
Checks battery voltage for a pre-dawn anomaly.
Identifies simultaneous steps, noise, or dropouts across channels with falling battery voltage as a possible power brownout.

Recognizes a salinity or specific-conductance decrease near an outfall as part of the marine stormwater pattern. Recognizes the turbidity spike coinciding with rain as a stormwater discriminator. Identifies lower pH as part of the marine stormwater pattern.
Notes that stormwater can carry bacteria, metals, and hydrocarbons.
States that DataPods cannot measure the metals in stormwater. Declines to supply a metals concentration from those pod measurements.
Describes a turbidity spike as a loading proxy rather than a measured metals concentration.
Keeps the instrument out of use until the error is identified, understood, and corrected.
Replaces the damaged sensor. Recalibrates after replacement.
Dries the sensor port before replacing the sensor. Offers compressed air for drying the port.
Keeps alcohol and other solvents away from the optical DO sensing surface because they can destroy it. Warns that solvents can also damage some plastics and o-rings.
Requires the underlying error to be identified, understood, and corrected before use.
Requires replacement of a damaged sensor. Requires recalibration after sensor replacement.
Recalibrates after replacing the damaged sensor.
Compares an abrupt offset in a serviced channel with the maintenance timestamp and log.
Maintains calibration records in the appropriate instrument or sensor logbook.
Inspects cables for damage. Inspects connectors and sensor ports for corrosion.
Uses cable coils no tighter than 6 inches in diameter. Stores cables clean and dry.
Checks that the correct measurement units are selected. Inspects connectors for moisture, dirt, or damage. Checks for loose connections.
